studies.label: Online experiment: coffee-mug idea generation with ChatGPT vs Google Search

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 11, Section 4, recruitment and attention-check exclusions
counts_source.quote: One hundred MTurk workers participated in the experiment. ... Ten participants who failed attention checks were removed. Our final sample comprised 90 participants, with 45 for each tool.

arms.name: LLM (ChatGPT)
arms.description: Participants used an embedded AI Assistant chat panel calling OpenAI's Chat Completion API with GPT-3.5-turbo; it retained recent conversation history and allowed starting a new conversation. Participants were instructed to use only the assigned tool.

arms.name: Search Engine (Google Search)
arms.description: Participants used an embedded search panel calling Google's Custom Search JSON API, with search results and visited pages displayed inside the panel. The task description and submission form matched the LLM condition.

studies.task: Generate up to five novel product ideas for coffee mugs using the assigned embedded tool.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT via OpenAI Chat Completion API, GPT-3.5-turbo
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 4; the model release year is not stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration is stated in the manuscript or Appendix A.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Items: novel, original, and exciting. MTurk raters evaluated six randomly selected ideas on a seven-point Likert scale; scores were normalized into z-scores within evaluator. Relevant item scores were averaged for each idea, then each participant received the mean score across their valid ideas. Both arms were evaluated using ChatGPT summaries of at most ten words, checked against original submissions by two postgraduate students. PDF pp. 12-13, Section 5.1; PDF p. 16, Section 5.2.3.

stats.difference_is: LLM minus Search Engine, as printed in the Difference column.

estimates.notes: One-way ANOVA compares participant-level outcomes. F degrees of freedom, arm SDs/SEs, difference SEs/CIs, and standardized effects are not printed; none were derived. The source quote for n_total also preserves the complete Table 2 descriptive row, whose columns are Obs, Mean, Median, STD, P25, and P75. Its STD describes the combined analysis sample, not either arm or a within-arm pooled SD, and is not entered as an arm SD. Printed decimal precision is retained in the source quotes. The rated and embedded comparisons include participants with at least one valid idea, a restriction after random assignment. They are not complete intention-to-treat analyses (PDF pp. 12, 16, and 20). Table 3 prints Difference 0.018 beside means 0.010 and -0.057; the printed difference is inconsistent with those means and is retained unchanged. Table 2 may have interchanged the Idea Novelty and Functional Appropriateness labels; its values are preserved as labeled in the source quote without relabeling or using its STD as a confirmed standardizer. Reconciliation audit: PDF p. 16 defines the participant mean of ratings of valid ideas, confirming unit=participant and se_basis=participant; the rated items support the recorded construct and more_creative direction. PDF p. 20 gives the analysis counts, independently checked against PDF pp. 12 and 17. These are the main available-case arm comparisons, not the separate tool-user regressions. Reconciliation audit: PDF p. 9 describes one assigned tool beside the idea-submission form, confirming immediate output production with AI available in the treatment arm and a between-person contrast (outcome_with_ai=true; within_person=null).

estimates.outcome: Divergent Thinking (semantic divergence of ideas within condition)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: For each idea, one minus the average cosine similarity of its embedding to all other ideas from participants within the same condition; these idea scores are averaged within participant. Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002, applied to the checked ChatGPT summaries. Higher scores indicate greater semantic divergence across people. PDF pp. 12-13, Section 5.1; PDF p. 17, Section 5.2.3 and footnote 10.

sources.quote: participants in the LLM condition generated more diverse ideas than those in the Search Engine condition (0.134 vs. 0.123, p < 0.01).

estimates.notes: One-way ANOVA compares participant-level outcomes. F degrees of freedom, arm SDs/SEs, difference SEs/CIs, and standardized effects are not printed; none were derived. The source quote for n_total also preserves the complete Table 2 descriptive row, whose columns are Obs, Mean, Median, STD, P25, and P75. Its STD describes the combined analysis sample, not either arm or a within-arm pooled SD, and is not entered as an arm SD. Printed decimal precision is retained in the source quotes. The rated and embedded comparisons include participants with at least one valid idea, a restriction after random assignment. They are not complete intention-to-treat analyses (PDF pp. 12, 16, and 20). The paper calls this Divergent Thinking, but it compares ideas across participants and is coded diversity/across_people. The comparison pool is defined separately within each condition. It is unclear whether a participant's own other ideas or invalid ideas enter the reference pool. Table 2 repeats the Functional Appropriateness row verbatim for this outcome and has a negative overall mean incompatible with the positive arm means in Table 3; no corrected summary was inferred. The sentence on PDF p. 17 saying tool nonusers have missing divergence conflicts with Table 3: its divergence counts exceed its tool-user counts. The counts recorded here follow the outcome row. The ANOVA uses participant averages; it does not report an adjustment for their shared reference pools. Footnote 10 says TF-IDF embeddings yield consistent results but prints no separate arm levels or uncertainty. Reconciliation audit: PDF p. 17 defines one minus cosine similarity against other ideas within condition and then averages each participant’s idea scores. This confirms question=across_people, construct=diversity, unit=participant, and higher_is=more_diverse. PDF p. 20 supplies the outcome-specific analysis counts; its F test treats participant averages as observations. Reconciliation audit: PDF p. 9 describes one assigned tool beside the idea-submission form, confirming immediate output production with AI available in the treatment arm and a between-person contrast (outcome_with_ai=true; within_person=null).

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Number of valid coffee-mug ideas submitted per participant. Two postgraduate students screened relevance and duplicates; repeated ideas from the same person were retained once. Ordinarily only the first idea in an input box was retained, but additional ideas could count when other boxes lacked valid ideas. Maximum five ideas. open_items: PDF p. 20, Table 3: the Idea Novelty Difference cell is inconsistent with the two arm means. All three values are transcribed as printed; the intended difference needs confirmation.

PDF p. 17, Table 2: Idea Novelty and Functional Appropriateness summary rows may be mislabeled. Their printed overall summaries conflict with the pattern of arm means in Table 3. Corrected labels and SDs are needed; no rows were swapped.
PDF p. 17, Table 2: the Divergent Thinking summary duplicates Functional Appropriateness and has an overall mean incompatible with its Table 3 arm means. A confirmed divergence SD is absent.

No participant-level arm SDs, arm SEs, unadjusted difference SEs/CIs, or F degrees of freedom are printed for the main comparisons. Appendix coefficients and SEs adjust for post-treatment variables and cannot fill those gaps.
PDF p. 11, Section 4: the per-arm allocation before attention-check exclusions and the per-arm exclusion counts are unreported.
PDF pp. 12, 16, and 20: rated-output and divergence analyses condition on having a valid idea after treatment. The study does not report full randomized-sample versions of these outcome contrasts.

PDF p. 17, Section 5.2.3: the assertion that tool nonusers lack divergence scores conflicts with the Table 3 outcome and tool-user counts. The actual divergence analysis sample needs confirmation; extraction follows Table 3 Panel C.
PDF p. 17, Section 5.2.3: the divergence reference set is all other ideas in the same condition, but inclusion of the participant's own other ideas and invalid submissions is not explicit.

PDF p. 16, Section 5.2.3: recruited rater count, ideas assigned per rater, and mean raters per idea do not reconcile with the valid-idea total on PDF p. 12. Final rater and rating counts and the evaluated idea set are unconfirmed.

Participant country, model release year, preregistration, and a preregistered primary outcome are not stated. No participant data or code link is provided. Exact manuscript revision date and latest-version status are unconfirmed.
Appendix A (PDF pp. 33-37) does not print model-specific participant counts. These mediator-adjusted models are excluded and cannot supply the counts or uncertainty for the main outcome contrasts.
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-10. The entire markdown conversion was read in consecutive chunks through the references and Appendix A. Every PDF page cited for the extracted numbers, outcome definitions, design, and exclusions was checked using PyMuPDF text extraction; PDF and printed page numbers coincide. The two study-field differences in the comparison file are resolved below. There are no unmatched estimates. All five screening outcomes and their ChatGPT-versus-Google Search contrasts are retained; none was added or removed. Counts, question, construct, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai, and within_person were independently checked against the PDF for every estimate, despite extractor agreement. The study randomized one hundred MTurk participants, analyzed ninety after attention-check exclusions, and prints no per-arm randomized allocation. The main analyses of rated quality and divergence have outcome-related missingness, recorded in the estimate notes and open_items. The separate tool-user regressions and all mediator-adjusted analyses are excluded. Table 2 descriptive rows are preserved as printed in the n_total source quotes; their overall SDs are not treated as arm-specific or within-arm pooled SDs. The screening form identifies no shared sample. The manuscript states no preregistration, primary outcome, participant country, or model release year. Source quotations preserve printed numerical precision. No effect, standard error, degree of freedom, or corrected table entry was calculated.
